classification.difficultyReason: Form equivalent equations, eliminate a variable and substitute to obtain exact fractional solutions.

content.prompt: Solve each pair of simultaneous equations.

answer.worked:
Multiply the second equation by $3$ and add it to the first:
$$\begin{align*}3x-3y&=18\\(5x+3y)+(3x-3y)&=15+18\\8x&=33\\x&=\frac{33}{8}\end{align*}$$
Substitute into $x-y=6$:
$$\begin{align*}\frac{33}{8}-y&=6\\-y&=\frac{15}{8}\\y&=-\frac{15}{8}\end{align*}$$
Check both original equations:
$$\begin{align*}5\left(\frac{33}{8}\right)+3\left(-\frac{15}{8}\right)&=15\\\frac{33}{8}-\left(-\frac{15}{8}\right)&=6\end{align*}$$

Multiply the first equation by $15$:
$$\begin{align*}5x+3y&=15\end{align*}$$
Multiply this equation by $5$ and the second original equation by $3$, then subtract:
$$\begin{align*}25x+15y&=75\\9x+15y&=45\\(25x+15y)-(9x+15y)&=75-45\\16x&=30\\x&=\frac{15}{8}\end{align*}$$
Substitute into $3x+5y=15$:
$$\begin{align*}3\left(\frac{15}{8}\right)+5y&=15\\5y&=\frac{75}{8}\\y&=\frac{15}{8}\end{align*}$$
Check both original equations:
$$\begin{align*}\frac{15/8}{3}+\frac{15/8}{5}&=\frac{5}{8}+\frac{3}{8}=1\\3\left(\frac{15}{8}\right)+5\left(\frac{15}{8}\right)&=15\end{align*}$$
